question: Do native post-activation FFN neuron axes support held-out perturbation selectivity at single/few-feature budgets beyond orthogonal rotations, PCA, residual coordinates and actual input?
design: 16 fresh synthetic backgrounds8/8 plus8 reused real4/4 when past-only artifacts exist; five RMS.1 perturbation types with sign/phase variants; background-locked normalization; first/half FFN and residual captures

interpretation: Eight held-out synthetic groups: Bolt first FFN RMS budget4 classification accuracy0.825, three-rotation mean0.525, PCA0.5750000000000001, actual-input0.925. Response purity0.5061468583439263 versus rotation mean0.29537045132605433 and PCA0.3185194702128912.
Bolt first FFN RMS budget1 has purity0.4248037916661324 versus PCA0.42658816064842653; no across-control single-neuron superiority claim.

TimesFM first FFN RMS budget4 synthetic classification0.7 versus rotations0.7833333333333333, PCA0.75, input0.925; purity0.5324001951242872 versus rotations0.46360563866441495 and PCA0.4913277537604803. These are different endpoints, not a uniform native-axis advantage.
Four reused real TEST groups are reported separately; TimesFM classification differs from the synthetic pattern, so source dependence is material.
FIT-selected Bolt units prefer ramprecent64/ramprecent64/noise/noise; TimesFM units prefer sin19.2/sin24/noise/noise. Preferences are restricted to this five-type contrast set.

First/half sites, mean/RMS views, all1/4/16 budgets and all three individual rotations remain in analysis and compact records; highlighted first-RMS results are descriptive, not a TEST-selected deployment rule.
